items.title: Kauffman bracket state sum
items.statement:
The input is a nonempty unoriented regular link diagram $D$: a finite immersed
planar projection of one or more circles with finitely many transverse double
points, no triple points, and over/under data at each double point. Let $C(D)$
be its finite crossing set. At each crossing take the local chart in which the
over-strand runs southwest to northeast and is drawn continuously over the
under-strand, which runs northwest to southeast with a gap at the intersection.
The A-smoothing joins the two left endpoints and the two right endpoints, with
weight $A$; the B-smoothing joins the two top endpoints and the two bottom
endpoints, with weight $A^{-1}$. These labels are transported with
orientation-preserving changes of local coordinates. Put
$\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$. The output is the Laurent polynomial $\langle D\rangle$.

1. Set an accumulator $p:=0$ in $\mathbb Z[A^{\pm1}]$.
2. For each function $S:C(D)\to\{A,B\}$, smooth every crossing according to
   $S$, obtaining a crossingless diagram with $|S|$ circles. Count the A- and
   B-smoothings as $a(S)$ and $b(S)$, and replace
   $$p\quad\text{by}\quad p+A^{a(S)-b(S)}\delta^{|S|-1}.$$
3. Return $p$ after all states have been processed.

The input is a mathematical diagram object, not a serialized string. The
procedure specifies no parsing or malformed-string rejection behavior. Since
the diagram has at least one component, every complete smoothing has
$|S|\ge1$ and every exponent of $\delta$ is nonnegative.

items.title: Kauffman bracket state-sum procedure properties
items.statement:
Let $A$ be an indeterminate and let $D$ be a typed nonempty unoriented regular
link diagram with finite crossing set $C(D)$. At each crossing use the chart
with the over-strand southwest-to-northeast: A joins the left endpoints and the
right endpoints with weight $A$, while B joins the top endpoints and bottom
endpoints with weight $A^{-1}$. The Kauffman bracket state-sum algorithm
terminates after exactly $2^{|C(D)|}$ state visits and returns
$$\sum_{S:C(D)\to\{A,B\}}A^{a(S)-b(S)}(-A^2-A^{-2})^{|S|-1},$$
where $a(S)$ and $b(S)$ count the two smoothing types and $|S|$ counts the
circles in the smoothed diagram. The algorithm takes a mathematical diagram
as input and makes no claim about parsing strings or rejecting malformed
encodings.

items.title: The normalized bracket is an oriented link invariant
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $A$ be an indeterminate and let $D$
be a nonempty regular oriented link diagram in an oriented $3$-sphere. Fix a
unit viewing normal $n$ and orient the projection plane $P$ so $(u,v)$ is
positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is positive in the ambient $3$-space. At each
crossing define $\operatorname{sgn}(c)=\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},
v_{\rm under})$ from the oriented projected tangents and set
$\operatorname{wr}(D)=\sum_c\operatorname{sgn}(c)$. At each crossing use the
local source chart in which the over-strand runs southwest to northeast; the
A-smoothing joins the left endpoints and the right endpoints with weight $A$,
and the B-smoothing joins the top endpoints and the bottom endpoints with
weight $A^{-1}$. Labels are transported by orientation-preserving changes of
local coordinates. Let $C(D)$ be the finite crossing set. A state is a map
$S:C(D)\to\{A,B\}$; let $a(S)$ and $b(S)$ count its A- and B-smoothings, and
let $|S|$ be the number of circles after all crossings are smoothed. Set
$$\langle D\rangle= \sum_{S:C(D)\to\{A,B\}}A^{a(S)-b(S)}(-A^2-A^{-2})^{|S|-1}.$$
Define
$$f_D(A)=(-A^3)^{-\operatorname{wr}(D)}\langle D\rangle,$$
where $\operatorname{wr}(D)$ is the sum of the determinant signs of its
oriented crossings. If two such diagrams represent ambient-isotopic
oriented links, their $f_D(A)$ values are equal. Thus $f_D$ defines an
invariant of nonempty oriented links.

items.title: The bracket state sum matches the library Jones specialization
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $A$ and $t$ be formal variables and $K$ a
nonempty oriented link. At each crossing of a regular diagram $D$ use the
source chart with over-strand southwest-to-northeast: A joins left and right
endpoints with coefficient $A$, and B joins top and bottom endpoints with
coefficient $A^{-1}$. A state $S:C(D)\to\{A,B\}$ assigns one smoothing at every
crossing; let $a(S)$ and $b(S)$ count these choices and $|S|$ count the
resulting circles. Fix a unit viewing normal $n$ and orient the projection
plane $P$ so $(u,v)$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is positive in the
ambient oriented $3$-sphere. Define
$$\operatorname{sgn}(c)=\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under}), \qquad \operatorname{wr}(D)=\sum_c\operatorname{sgn}(c),$$
$$f_K(A)=(-A^3)^{-\operatorname{wr}(D)} \sum_{S:C(D)\to\{A,B\}}A^{a(S)-b(S)}(-A^2-A^{-2})^{|S|-1}.$$
For an $n$-strand braid $\beta$ whose oriented closure is $K$, let
$e:B_n\to\mathbb Z$ be the homomorphism $e(\sigma_i)=1$, where $\sigma_i$
is the positive geometric Artin half twist. Let $H(n)$ be the type-A Hecke
algebra with generators $T_i$, quadratic relation $T_i^2=(v-1)T_i+v$, braid
relations, and distant commutation, and let $\pi_n(\sigma_i)=T_i$. Its
normalized Markov trace $\operatorname{tr}_n$ satisfies
$\operatorname{tr}_n(1)=1$, cyclicity, tower restriction, and
$\operatorname{tr}_{n+1}(xT_n)=z\operatorname{tr}_n(x)$. Define the library
Jones value by
$$V_K(t)=s^{e(\beta)}\left(-\frac{s^2+1}{s}\right)^{n-1} \operatorname{tr}_n(\pi_n(\beta))\Big|_{v=s^2,\,z=-1/(s^2+1),\,t=s^2},$$
where $s=t^{1/2}$. With $A=t^{-1/4}$, these values satisfy
$$V_K(t)=f_K(t^{-1/4}).$$

items.title: Trefoil, mirror, and unknot bracket calculations
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $A$ be an indeterminate. Let $D_+$ be the
positive trefoil diagram, defined
as the closure of the two-strand braid $\sigma_1^3$, where $\sigma_1$ is the
anticlockwise geometric half twist with the left label passing below and the
right label above the midpoint, and both strands are oriented in the braid
direction. Let $D_-$ be its mirror image, and let $U$ be the crossing-free
one-component unknot diagram. Fix a unit viewing normal $n$ and orient the
projection plane $P$ so $(u,v)$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is positive
in the oriented ambient $3$-space. At each crossing use the local source chart
whose over-strand runs southwest to northeast; the A-smoothing joins the left
endpoints and right endpoints with weight $A$, and the B-smoothing joins the
top endpoints and bottom endpoints with weight $A^{-1}$. Transport these
labels by orientation-preserving changes of local coordinates. For a diagram
$D$, let $C(D)$ be its finite crossing set. Each state is a map
$S:C(D)\to\{A,B\}$; let $a(S)$ and $b(S)$ count the smoothing types and $|S|$
count its circles. Define
$\langle D\rangle=\sum_{S:C(D)\to\{A,B\}}
A^{a(S)-b(S)}(-A^2-A^{-2})^{|S|-1}$ and
$f_D(A)=(-A^3)^{-\operatorname{wr}(D)}\langle D\rangle$, where writhe is the
sum of determinant crossing signs, computed as
$\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$ after fixing a unit
viewing normal $n$ and using the induced orientation of $P$ above. With
$t=A^{-4}$ and Jones polynomial
$V_D(t)=f_D(t^{-1/4})$, the values are
$$V_{D_+}(t)=t+t^3-t^4,\qquad V_{D_-}(t)=t^{-1}+t^{-3}-t^{-4},\qquad V_U(t)=1.$$

items.title: A type-I kink changes the raw bracket
items.statement:
The false statement is: let $A$ be an indeterminate and, for every nonempty
regular oriented diagram $D$ of an unframed knot with finite crossing set
$C(D)$, let
$$\langle D\rangle=\sum_{S:C(D)\to\{A,B\}} A^{a(S)-b(S)}(-A^2-A^{-2})^{|S|-1},$$
where $a(S)$ and $b(S)$ count A- and B-smoothings, the over-strand runs
southwest to northeast, A joins the left and right endpoint pairs with weight
$A$, B joins the top and bottom endpoint pairs with weight $A^{-1}$, and
$|S|$ is the number of state circles. Then
$\langle D\rangle$ depends only on the
ambient-isotopy class of the represented oriented knot.

items.title: Framed link diagrams and local Reidemeister moves in plane products
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal A$ be a smooth planar
annulus and let $X=\mathcal A\times(-1,1)$, the interior of a solid torus.
A regular annular diagram is a finite immersed union of circles in
$\operatorname{int}(\mathcal A)$ with only finitely many transverse double
points, no triple points, and over/under data from the interval coordinate.
The **blackboard framing** is the normal strip lying in the annulus. A specified
framing differs from it on each component by an integer full-twist correction,
measured by the winding number of its normal direction relative to the
blackboard normal. Count the correction positively for an A-type full twist,
whose local curl has A-smoothing equal to the straight strip with one
contractible circle; count the opposite B-type twist negatively. Every framed
link in $X$ admits a regular annular diagram. The correction may be recorded
as signed full-twist marks on diagram arcs; its total is additive when arcs
are concatenated.

If two framed links in $X$ are ambient isotopic through links in $X$, their
regular annular diagrams are related by finitely many annular planar isotopies
and local oriented Reidemeister I, II, and III moves in disks contained in
$\operatorname{int}(\mathcal A)$. Reidemeister II and III and planar isotopy
preserve the blackboard framing; an A-type or B-type Reidemeister I move
changes it by one corresponding full twist, so the correction integer changes
by the opposite twist. For framed links in $S^3$, every link also admits a
regular planar diagram, and any two diagrams of ambient-isotopic framed links
are related by a finite planar-isotopy/Reidemeister sequence with the same
framing-correction rule.

items.title: Kauffman regular-isotopy and Dubrovnik conventions
items.statement:
Let
$$R_D=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},z,d^{\pm1}]/(z(d-1)-(a-a^{-1})),$$
where $z$ is not inverted. A nonempty unoriented regular link diagram is a
finite generic planar projection of one or more circles with only transverse
double crossings and an over/under marking at each crossing. Use the crossing
chart in which the over-strand runs southwest to northeast. Its $D_0$
smoothing joins the left endpoints and the right endpoints (the through
pairing), and its $D_\infty$ smoothing joins the two top endpoints and the two
bottom endpoints (the cup-cap pairing). Thus $D_0$ is the orientation-preserving
smoothing when both crossing strands point downward and the displayed crossing
has positive determinant sign. These are respectively the $A$- and
$B$-smoothings in the stated bracket chart. A positive
curl is a type-I kink whose oriented crossing has determinant sign $+1$; a
negative curl has determinant sign $-1$. The sign is unchanged if the
orientation of the whole component is reversed.

The Dubrovnik regular-isotopy evaluation $P$ is normalized by
$P(\varnothing)=1$, $P(K\sqcup\bigcirc)=dP(K)$, positive and negative curl
factors $a$ and $a^{-1}$, and
$$P(D_+)-P(D_-)=z\bigl(P(D_0)-P(D_\infty)\bigr).$$
Here $D_+$ and $D_-$ differ only by switching the displayed crossing. For a
nonempty oriented link diagram $K$, let $c(K)$ be its number of components and
let $w(K)$ be the sum of the determinant crossing signs. Define
$$D_K(a,z)=d^{-1}P(K),$$
$$L_K(A,Z)=-i^{w(K)}(-1)^{c(K)}D_K(-iA,iZ),\qquad i^2=-1,$$
and
$$F_K(A,Z)=A^{-w(K)}L_K(A,Z).$$
Thus $D$ has unknot value $1$, and the universal relation defining $R_D$ is
retained even when $z$ is not invertible. These are conventions and
normalizations; ambient-isotopy invariance of $F$ is a separate theorem.

items.title: BMW relations in the Dubrovnik parameter convention
items.statement:
Let
$$S=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},z,d^{\pm1}]/(z(d-1)-(a-a^{-1}))$$
be the Dubrovnik coefficient ring, and let
$$T=S[q^{\pm1}]/(q-q^{-1}-z).$$
In $T$ put $\rho=a$, $\delta=d$, and $z_B=q-q^{-1}$. Then the natural
map $S\to T$ is injective and $T$ is a free $S$-module with basis $1,q$.
Moreover, the BMW coefficient relation
$$z_B(\delta-1)=\rho-\rho^{-1}$$
holds, and the substitution $a=\rho$, $z_D=z_B$, $d=\delta$ converts
the BMW skein, curl, adjacent untwisting, and loop coefficients to the
Dubrovnik relations in the specified chart: $D_+-D_-=z_D(D_0-D_\infty)$,
the curl factors are $a,a^{-1}$, and a disjoint trivial circle contributes
$d$. Here $D_0$ is through and $D_\infty$ is cup-cap. No skein parameter is
divided out.

items.title: The BMW presentation maps to the Dubrovnik tangle algebra
items.statement: Let $T$ be the coefficient extension and parameter substitution in the BMW-to-Dubrovnik dictionary, and let $\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$ be the ordinary Dubrovnik tangle skein algebra: its diagrams are finite generic projections of $n$ arcs with fixed ordered top and bottom endpoints and closed curves, modulo planar isotopy, Reidemeister II and III, the Dubrovnik skein relation, the two curl relations, and the free-circle relation with parameters $z_D,a,a^{-1},d$. In its fixed chart, $D_0$ is through left/right and $D_\infty$ is cup-cap top/bottom. For every $n\ge2$, send the BMW generator $g_i$ to the positive Artin crossing between strands $i,i+1$, its inverse to the negative crossing, and $e_i$ to the adjacent cup-cap tangle. This assignment extends to a unital $T$-algebra homomorphism $\Phi_n:BMW_n(T;q,\rho,\delta)\to\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$. For $n=0,1$, define the unital $T$-algebra homomorphism by sending each scalar to that scalar times the empty or straight tangle, respectively. This claim asserts well-definedness only; it does not assert surjectivity or injectivity.

items.title: The fundamental quantum sl2 ribbon trace matches the Hecke and bracket evaluations
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $A$ be an indeterminate, $q_K=A^2$, $q_L=A^{-2}$, and $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$. Use the fundamental module, positive crossing, duality maps, and twist fixed in the preceding definition. For every $n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$, let $t_n(\beta)$ be the categorical ribbon trace of its blackboard-framed closure and let $w(\beta)$ be its exponent sum. With $t=A^{-4}$ and $z_0=-1/(t+1)$, the exact identities are
$$t_n(\beta)=\delta\langle\widehat\beta\rangle=\delta^n(-A)^{w(\beta)}\operatorname{tr}_n(\pi_n(\beta))\big|_{v=t,\ z=z_0},$$
$$(-A^3)^{-w(\beta)}t_n(\beta)=\delta(-A^3)^{-w(\beta)}\langle\widehat\beta\rangle.$$
Here $\operatorname{tr}_n$ is the normalized type-A Hecke Markov trace with braid generator sent to $T_i$, and $\langle\widehat\beta\rangle$ is the Kauffman bracket in the fixed crossing chart. The second identity is a value-by-value normalization formula; it does not by itself assert a Jones-polynomial specialization.

items.title: Bracket smoothings of positive and negative braid crossings
Hecke–bracket trace dictionary and local descent
items.statement:
Let $A$ be an indeterminate, $R_A=\mathbb Z[A^{\pm1},(A^{-4}+1)^{-1}]$,
$q=A^{-2}$, $t=q^2=A^{-4}$, $\delta=-(q+q^{-1})=-A^2-A^{-2}$, and
$z_0=-1/(t+1)$. For a nonempty regular diagram $D$, define
$\langle D\rangle$ by summing its crossing smoothings with weights $A$ and
$A^{-1}$ and the factor $\delta^{k-1}$ for a state with $k$ circles. Let
$B_n$ be the $n$-strand Artin braid group with positive geometric generators
$\sigma_i$ (label $i$ passes below the midpoint and label $i+1$ passes above),
drawn with braid parameter increasing from bottom to top; let
$e:B_n\to\mathbb Z$ be the homomorphism $e(\sigma_i)=1$. Let $H(n)$ be
the type-A Hecke algebra with generators $T_i$, quadratic relation
$T_i^2=(v-1)T_i+v$, braid relations, and distant commutation; let $\pi_n$
send $\sigma_i$ to $T_i$. Its normalized Markov trace $\operatorname{tr}_n$
satisfies $\operatorname{tr}_n(1)=1$, cyclicity, tower restriction, and
$\operatorname{tr}_{n+1}(xT_n)=z\operatorname{tr}_n(x)$. Let
$\mathrm{TL}_n$ be the noncrossing pairing algebra with loop value $\delta$,
and let $\operatorname{Tr}_n(D)=\delta^{c(D)}$ be the unnormalized trace,
where $c(D)$ is the number of circles after joining corresponding top and
bottom endpoints outside the rectangle; set
$\tau_n=\delta^{-n}\operatorname{Tr}_n$. For $\beta\in B_n$,
$n\ge1$, orient its closure in the braid direction. Under the specialization
$v\mapsto t$, $z\mapsto z_0$ of the Hecke tower, one has
$$\langle\widehat\beta\rangle =\delta^{n-1}(-A)^{e(\beta)}\operatorname{tr}_n(\pi_n(\beta))\big|_{v=t,\,z=z_0}.$$
The identity gives bracket value $1$ on the one-strand identity closure. Its
positive and negative Markov stabilizations multiply the raw bracket by
$-A^3$ and $-A^{-3}$, respectively.

items.title: Kauffman bracket R2 and R3 identities
Kauffman bracket skein module of a three-manifold
A formal third Reidemeister equivalence from explicit residual saddles
items.statement:
Assume countable choice. Put six points on a disk boundary in clockwise order $1,2,3,4,5,6$, at northwest, northeast, east, southeast, southwest and west. Consider diagonal arcs $a$ from $1$ to $4$ and $b$ from $2$ to $5$, and an arc $c$ from $6$ to $3$. In the left diagram $c$ bows above the intersection of $a,b$; in the right it bows below. In both diagrams $c$ passes over both diagonals. Either $a$ passes over $b$ in both diagrams, or $b$ passes over $a$ in both. These are the two local third Reidemeister variants considered here. More precisely one can use the diameters $y=-x,y=x$ for $a,b$ and the curves $y=\pm h(1-x^2)$, $0<h<1/2$, for $c$, with fixed radial collars near the six boundary points.

Use the local smoothing chart in which the over-strand joins southwest to northeast and the under-strand joins northwest to southeast. The A-smoothing joins the left pair and right pair, and the B-smoothing joins the top pair and bottom pair. An A-first cube uses $0=A,1=B$; a B-first cube uses $0=B,1=A$. For either convention, the raw formal cube of an ordered diagram has term $\bigoplus_{|v|=s}S_v\{s\}$ in cochain degree $s$ and edge saddle coefficient $(-1)^{\sum_{k<j}v_k}$ in coordinate $j$. For any choice of strand orientations, put this term in degree $s-n_-$ and shift it internally by the additional $n_+-2n_-$.

For each of these two smoothing conventions, the formal cubes of the two diagrams admit internal degree zero chain homotopy equivalences, with explicit maps given below. The displayed smoothing table and cone calculation use A-first cubes: turning right from an entering underpassing half-line gives the A-smoothing. The B-first maps are obtained from the raw A-first maps by complementing every bit and reversing surface time, without spatial reflection, with the explicit vertex sign correction below; only after this operation are the same given $n_+,n_-$ normalizations applied to both sides. All these maps and homotopies can be inserted into any planar surrounding complex.

items.title: Exact bracket output bit-growth bound
items.statement:
Let $D$ be a nonempty unoriented regular link diagram with $c$ crossings and $m\ge1$ components, and let $\langle D\rangle=\sum_j z_jA^j$ be its exact Kauffman bracket. Its Laurent exponents satisfy $|j|\le 3c+2m-2$, and its signed-magnitude coefficient-bit size, as defined in the encoded diagram size definition, is at most $m+2c+1$. Consequently, a knot diagram ($m=1$) has Laurent degree and coefficient-bit size bounded linearly in $c+1$.

The state-sum algorithm admits a naive exact implementation taking
$O(2^c(c+m+1)^4)$ elementary bit steps in the following model. Its typed
input gives $c$ and the number $u$ of crossingless components in
self-delimiting binary: each number is encoded by $b$ ones, a zero, and its
$b$ ordinary binary digits, with $b\ge1$ the number of those digits.
These fields are followed by the edge-pairing table on the $4c$
endpoints indexed by crossing and local port. Its entries are ordered by
endpoint index and each uses $\max(1,\lceil\log_2(4c+1)\rceil)$ bits.
At each crossing the ports are northwest, northeast,
southeast, southwest in the bracket's fixed local chart; the two smoothing
pairings are therefore fixed pairs of port indices. The table is assumed to
be the incidence data of the given diagram. Polynomial arithmetic uses dense
arrays of signed binary integer coefficients, and one tape-cell read, write,
or head move on a fixed finite number of binary work tapes costs one step.
For knots this bound is $O(2^c(c+1)^4)$. It is a bound for this explicit
indexed implementation, not for arbitrary black-box polynomial operations.
Constructing the indexed input from an arbitrary literal code of length $L$,
reading other labels or padding, and processing geometric coordinates are
outside this bound.

items.title: Lee filtered homology is an oriented link invariant
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. If $D$ and $D'$ are finite regular diagrams of the same nonempty oriented link, then their rational Lee cochain complexes are related by a cochain homotopy equivalence whose maps and homotopies preserve the decreasing quantum filtrations after normalization. Consequently their Lee homology groups with induced filtrations are isomorphic, and the spectral sequences from the rational Khovanov page onward are isomorphic. These filtered groups and pages therefore depend only on the oriented link.

items.title: Reduced Khovanov ranks of the unknot and the three-crossing two-braid
Kauffman bracket smoothing and loop value
The fundamental quantum sl2 module in the Kauffman-bracket ribbon convention
items.statement:
Let $\omega$ be an indeterminate, set $A=\omega^{-2}$, and put $k'=\mathbb Q(\omega)$, $q_K=A^2$, and $q_L=A^{-2}$. Work over the scalar extension to $k'$ of the library Hopf algebra at $q_L$; $U_{q_K}$ in Korinman's convention is identified by $q_L=q_K^{-1}$ and $K_L=K_K^{-1}$. Use its generic two-dimensional module $V$ over $k'$ with ordered basis $(v_+,v_-)$ and generator matrices
$$E=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad F=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad K_K=\begin{pmatrix}q_K&0\\0&q_K^{-1}\end{pmatrix}.$$
Equivalently, for the library parameter $q_L=q_K^{-1}$ use $K_L=K_K^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(q_L,q_L^{-1})$ and the library coproduct convention $\Delta(E)=E\otimes K_L^{-1}+1\otimes E$, $\Delta(F)=F\otimes1+K_L\otimes F$. This parameter and Cartan-generator conversion is part of the definition; the two $q$ symbols are not identified.

The object $V$ is absolutely simple in the $k'$-linear representation category.

Equip $V$ with the Kauffman-bracket half-ribbon structure. The half-ribbon operator $\Omega$ is specified by
$$C:=\operatorname{Mat}_{(v_+,v_-)}(\Omega^{-1})=\begin{pmatrix}0&\omega\\-\omega^5&0\end{pmatrix},$$
and its associated twist is $\theta_V=\Omega^2=-A^3\operatorname{id}_V$. In the ordered basis $(v_+\otimes v_+,v_+\otimes v_-,v_-\otimes v_+,v_-\otimes v_-)$, the positive braiding is
$$c_{V,V}=\begin{pmatrix}A&0&0&0\\0&0&A^{-1}&0\\0&A^{-1}&A-A^{-3}&0\\0&0&0&A\end{pmatrix}.$$
Its ribbon quantum dimension is $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$. The half-ribbon and universal $R$-matrix are those of the topological half-ribbon representation category; the selected ribbon element is the Kauffman-bracket one, not the usual $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ ribbon element.

Let $v_+^*,v_-^*$ be the ordinary dual basis. The left-dual action on $V^*$ is the contragredient action $(x\cdot f)(v)=f(S(x)v)$ for the antipode $S$ of the stated library Hopf convention. Identify the displayed copy of $V$ with this left dual $V^\vee$ by $v_+\mapsto v_-^*$ and $v_-\mapsto -A^{-2}v_+^*$. In this identification the evaluation and coevaluation maps are
$$B(v_+\otimes v_-)=1,\quad B(v_-\otimes v_+)=-A^{-2},\quad B(v_+\otimes v_+)=B(v_-\otimes v_-)=0,$$
$$U(1)=-A^2v_+\otimes v_-+v_-\otimes v_+.$$
These are the explicit duality maps used in the closure trace.

The positive Artin generator is drawn with braid height increasing upward; the left input strand ends on the right, and the right input strand passes over it:

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(current bounding box.center),scale=.8]
  \draw[->] (0,-1) -- (.46,-.08);
  \draw[->] (.54,.08) -- (1,1);
  \draw[->] (1,-1) .. controls (.72,-.5) and (.28,.5) .. (0,1);
  \node at (-.2,-1) {$i$};
  \node at (1.2,-1) {$i+1$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

The uninterrupted strand in the drawing is the overpassing strand. This is the crossing convention for the displayed matrix; the proof below uses its matrix entries and the half-ribbon source formulas, not the drawing.

items.title: Based-link reduced Khovanov equivalences for every local Reidemeister move
items.statement: Let $(D,p)$ and $(D',p')$ be finite regular diagrams of nonempty oriented links related by a planar isotopy or one oriented Reidemeister move, with the marked point on an unchanged exterior arc and carried to the corresponding point. The normalized integral signed Khovanov complexes have explicit bigraded chain homotopy equivalences whose maps and inverse homotopies commute with the marked actions $X_p,X_{p'}$. Consequently the quotients $C(D)/\operatorname{im}X_p$ and $C(D')/\operatorname{im}X_{p'}$, with their reduced quantum degree $j-1$, are bigraded chain homotopy equivalent. The conclusion holds over $\mathbb F_2$ by reducing these same integral formulas. It permits arbitrary other link components and arbitrary exterior connectivity. This local statement does not assert a relative movie theorem or canonical identifications between different move sequences.

items.title: Reduced Khovanov homology over F2 is an oriented link invariant
items.statement: Assume ACω. For every nonempty oriented link $L\subset S^3$, the bigraded $\mathbb F_2$ vector spaces $\widetilde{Kh}^{i,j}(L;\mathbb F_2)$ obtained by reducing the normalized Khovanov complex at a point on any chosen component are independent, up to noncanonical bigraded isomorphism, of the diagram and the chosen component. No filtered structure from a Floer construction is part of this invariance statement.

items.title: The Khovanov to branched-cover Heegaard Floer spectral sequence
items.statement: Assume AC and ACω. For every nonempty oriented link $L\subset S^3$, there is a spectral sequence over $\mathbb F_2$ whose $E_2$ page is the reduced Khovanov cohomology $\widetilde{Kh}^{*,*}(\overline L;\mathbb F_2)$ of the mirror link and whose abutment is $\widehat{HF}(\Sigma(L);\mathbb F_2)$ with its image filtration. The page identification is an isomorphism of bigraded vector spaces; this statement does not claim a diagram-independent filtered quasi-isomorphism type for the chain-level spectral sequence.
